metric.semantic_determinacy.basis: per-probe B_i assigned by inspecting the frozen canonical_task's local surface form for Rust under the frozen toolchain recipe (rustc -O -C debug-assertions=on). A materially different interpretation changes mutation, aliasing, failure, conversion, dispatch, resource behavior, control flow, representation, or observable result, per spec 6.1.3.B. The glyph-neutrality rule (no bonus/penalty merely for '&') was applied.
caveats: B values reflect the single-language Rust shard only, per the assigned-languages restriction of this task packet.

Overflow-sensitive plain-operator sites (F03.P1, F07.P1, F16.P1) are scored B=2 because Rust's arithmetic-overflow behavior for the bare operator is genuinely compilation-profile dependent (cfg(debug_assertions)); this is distinct from Semantic Locality, which separately charges a compiler-mode lookup for the same fact.

Cross-language aggregation, common-basis vs all-fragments reconciliation, and comparability-gate determination are runner-only per the frozen packet policy and are not performed by this single-language worker.
metric.semantic_determinacy.methodology_citation: semantic_compression.md section B: raw value = mean(log2(B_i)) over the 44 fixed probes, where B_i is the count of materially different semantic interpretations compatible with the probe's local surface form alone, before consulting external declarations/signatures. Lower branching is better.
metric.semantic_determinacy.normalization: score = 100 * (1 - mean_log2B / CAP), clamped to [0,100]; CAP = 3 (log2(8)), chosen before language-specific computation as a language-neutral ceiling representing a probe with 8 materially distinct locally-compatible interpretations (the maximum branching enumerated anywhere in the fixed probe set, per F05.P1's own scoring note listing up to 6-8 candidate outcomes). This CAP is applied identically to every language shard.

per_probe.note: let n = 7; immutable-by-default binding, type inferred i32; fully determinate from local syntax alone.
static mut COUNTER vs const LIMIT: mutability explicit via keyword contrast.
let v: i32; with compiler-enforced definite assignment on both branches; single interpretation.
MaybeUninit<[u8;16]> explicitly signals genuinely uninitialized storage.
x += 1 on i32: overflow behavior (panic vs wrap) depends on cfg(debug_assertions)/opt-level, not visible at the bare operator site alone.
xs[1] = 42 on Vec<i32>: bounds-checked in-place write, deterministic panic-on-OOB semantics.
let port: &mut i32 = &mut slot; explicit writable-alias syntax fully announces mutation and aliasing.
let window: &[i32] = &xs[..]; explicit borrow, non-copying, read-only by type.
Rc<RefCell<..>> plus Rc::ptr_eq: explicit reference-identity operation distinct from PartialEq.

f(x) with x: Vec<i32> (non-Copy): Rust's move semantics make the call-site outcome determinate without the callee signature -- x is moved and the original binding becomes unusable, eliminating alternative aliasing/mutation outcomes.
put(cell: &mut i32) via put(&mut cell): explicit &mut fully announces writable aliasing.
closure `let neg = |a: i32| k - a;` passed by name to .map(neg): explicit closure type and capture.
mid returns i32 (Copy type); returned element is an independent copy, deterministic.
tuple return (i32, i32) with explicit destructuring let (q, r) = divmod2(a, b);
let r = a * b + c; overflow outcome (panic vs wrap) is build-profile dependent, not locally visible.
/ and % truncate toward zero and panic on zero-divisor deterministically; explicit `as f64` for real division.
m.checked_add(1) (rung i) yields Option<i32>, fully determinate at the site.
a.checked_div(b) (rung i) yields Option<i32>, fully determinate.
s1 == s2 on String: PartialEq is content equality by specification, not identity.
xs.sort_by(|a,b| b.cmp(a)): in-place mutation, explicit descending comparator.
big.try_into() (rung i) yields Result<i32,_>, out-of-range outcome explicit.
i as f64 + d: Rust has no implicit numeric conversions, explicit `as` required at the site.
xs[i]: Index trait panics deterministically on out-of-range.
&xs[1..4]: slice borrow, shares storage, non-copying by construction.
let o: Option<i32> = None; o.unwrap_or(0): fully explicit optionality and fallback.
o.map(h): standard optional-aware chaining, short-circuits on None deterministically.
fn parse_twice(s:&str)->Result<i32,ParseIntError> using s.parse::<i32>()? : explicit Result type and ? propagation.
match on Result explicitly handles Ok/Err locally.
enum Shape { Circle{r:f64}, Rect{w:f64,h:f64} }: enums are closed sum types by language rule.
match s { Shape::Circle{r}=>.., Shape::Rect{w,h}=>.. } with no wildcard: compiler-enforced exhaustiveness.
trait Shape { fn area(&self)->f64; } plus separate-module impl Shape for Tri: explicit impl blocks, dynamic dispatch via Box<dyn Shape>.
fn head<T: Clone>(xs: &[T]) -> T: explicit generic bound and declared return type T.
fn max_of<T: PartialOrd>(a:T,b:T)->T: constraint written at the declaration.
Vec<Box<dyn Named>>: explicit trait-object type, runtime dispatch signaled by dyn.
xs.iter().sum(): the summation's own overflow outcome is build-profile dependent, mirroring F03.P1/F07.P1.
HashMap<String,i32>: unordered iteration is documented language fact, not an ambiguity; get("b").copied().unwrap_or(0) is explicit.
std::fs::File Drop-based RAII with ? propagation guarantees release exactly once on every exit path.
struct Handle{id:i32} impl Drop for Handle: deterministic, exactly-once, scope-end cleanup.
println!("x"); via prelude macro, no import required, fully determinate.
mod util { pub fn pub_add.. ; fn secret() .. }: pub/private explicit at declaration.
std::thread::spawn + JoinHandle::join: explicit standard concurrency facility, deterministic join point.
Arc<Mutex<i64>>: explicit, documented race-free discipline at the mutation site.
extern "C" { fn abs(a: i32) -> i32; } called inside unsafe {}: explicit foreign boundary and unsafe marker.
#[no_mangle] pub extern "C" fn add2(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32: explicit ABI and export attributes.
